buzzRounds.topic: Rookie of the Year winners named
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Baseball Writers' Association of America named its Rookies of the Year on Monday, November 9. Tigers shortstop Kevin McGonigle won the American League award with 204 points and 28 of 30 first-place votes, ahead of Parker Messick's 122, and Reds first baseman Sal Stewart won the National League award after hitting 32 home runs.
buzzRounds.whyCare: CBS Sports notes Stewart is one of just 15 rookies ever with at least 30 home runs and 100 runs batted in, and the awards kick off a week that ends with Most Valuable Player on Thursday, November 12.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Kevin McGonigle won American League Rookie of the Year with 28 of 30 first-place votes, and Sal Stewart took the National League award after hitting 32 home runs as a Reds rookie.

buzzRounds.topic: Awards week: Cy Young and MVP are this week
buzzRounds.whatHappened: Baseball's big awards are announced this week: Manager of the Year on Tuesday, November 10, the Cy Young Awards (best pitcher) on Wednesday, November 11, and Most Valuable Player on Thursday, November 12. Brewers righty Jacob Misiorowski, a National League Cy Young finalist, led the majors with 252 strikeouts and a 1.80 earned run average, Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez is an American League MVP finalist after hitting .316 with 42 home runs, and Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is a National League MVP finalist after 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases.
buzzRounds.whyCare: ESPN notes Alvarez fell one home run and seven runs batted in short of a Triple Crown (leading the league in batting average, home runs and runs batted in), and the World Series champion Brewers have a Cy Young finalist and an MVP finalist in Brice Turang.

buzzRounds.whatHappened: The general managers' meetings opened Monday, November 9, in Las Vegas with no major deals yet, and reporter Jon Paul Morosi says team officials told him trade talks are more advanced than is typical for this point in November. MLB's labor contract expires December 1 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern, and the Associated Press reports MLB is likely to lock out the players when it does. buzzRounds.whyCare: The 2027 season is scheduled to start March 24, and the last lockout, in 2021-22, lasted 99 days, so teams may try to make moves before December 1.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Baseball's labor contract expires December 1 and a lockout, meaning owners stop the players from working, is expected, and reporter Jon Paul Morosi says trade talks at this week's general managers' meetings are further along than usual for November.

buzzRounds.topic: Mariners hire a manager who has never managed
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Mariners hired Jason Kanzler, 36, as manager on Tuesday, November 3. He was the Cubs' director of player development, has never managed at any level, and replaces Dan Wilson after Seattle went 76-86, a year after reaching Game 7 of the American League Championship Series.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Kanzler is the second-youngest manager in baseball behind the Nationals' Blake Butera, 34, and catcher Cal Raleigh hit .182 with 23 homers and 69 runs batted in for a Seattle offense that scored the third-fewest runs in the majors.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: The Mariners hired 36-year-old Jason Kanzler, who has never managed anywhere, after a 76-86 season. Catcher Cal Raleigh hit just .182 and Randy Arozarena got a qualifying offer, so he has until November 17 to decide.
